input: Members will wish to be aware that the position on programme has deteriorated further since the last update, and the overrun now stands at some 8 weeks against the programme reported to the project board. The root cause of the slippage has been traced to the main equipment package, where a series of difficulties in fabrication led to completion falling progressively behind the dates set out in the accepted programme, with the consequence that delivery to site ultimately missed the installation window which the package was intended to meet. Because a considerable amount of the follow-on work is dependent, directly or indirectly, on the package being in place, that work has effectively stood idle in sequence, and the 8-week overrun which is now reported represents the accumulated slippage at the current position rather than any allowance for further deterioration. By way of mitigation, it is proposed that the remaining installation work under the EPC contractor be resequenced, so that those areas which do not depend on the package are progressed first, whilst the installation of the package itself is compressed into a shorter window once delivery has taken place; the planning manager will own the resequencing and will report progress against it at each review. It should be noted that resequencing can be expected to recover only that part of the slip which idle sequencing has caused, and that the balance, which arises from the late delivery itself, can be recovered only insofar as the compressed window can be held. Acceptance of the resequencing rests with the project board, and until such time as the board accepts it, the programme continues to carry the overrun unmitigated, with the completion forecast remaining where the slippage places it.
target:
The overrun now stands at 8 weeks against the programme reported to the project board, and the cause sits with the main equipment package. Fabrication of the package finished behind the dates in the accepted programme, the slip growing at each successive report as the fabrication dates moved, and delivery to site missed the installation window the package was meant to meet. Work that depended on the package has stood idle in sequence, and the 8-week overrun is the accumulated slip at the current position, not a forecast of further delay. The overrun is stated against the accepted programme, the same basis as the last report, and no other workstream reports a slip of its own.

The mitigation proposed is a resequencing of the remaining installation work under the EPC contractor: areas that do not depend on the package proceed first, and the package installation is compressed into a shorter window once delivery lands. The planning manager owns the resequencing and reports progress against it at each review. The resequencing is drawn from the contractor's own remaining programme, reordered rather than extended, and it asks for no additional resources beyond the shifts already allowed for in the installation plan. Areas released early are those whose completion releases further work in turn, so the order is set by dependency rather than by convenience. Resequencing recovers the part of the slip that idle sequencing caused; the part caused by the late delivery itself is recovered only if the compressed window holds.

Acceptance of the resequencing rests with the project board. Until the board accepts it, the programme carries the overrun unmitigated, and the completion forecast stays where the slip puts it. What the resequencing cannot settle is the delivery date itself, which the contractor has confirmed verbally and not in writing.
